question: What is the main goal of a fasting blood sugar test?

options.A: To find out the percentage of red blood cells carrying oxygen
options.B: To check how quickly the kidneys filter waste products
options.C: To measure blood sugar levels after a period without eating
options.D: To check the total amount of protein stored in the liver

explanation: You've got this! A fasting blood sugar test simply looks at your glucose levels after you haven't eaten for a while, usually overnight. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h1)

question: When a patient fasts, how does the body keep blood sugar from dropping too low?

options.A: The liver stops all metabolic activity until the next meal
options.B: The pancreas releases extra insulin to store extra sugar
options.C: The muscles absorb all available glucose to build up fat stores
options.D: The pancreas releases glucagon to tell the liver to release stored sugar

explanation: Think of glucagon as the body's natural backup alarm! When food isn't coming in, glucagon tells the liver to share its stored glucose to keep your energy stable. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h1)

question: A fasting blood sugar test is most commonly used to check for which condition?
explanation: Spot on! Fasting blood sugar is one of the quickest and most common ways doctors and nurses screen for diabetes mellitus. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h2)

question: Which patient is the best candidate for a routine fasting blood sugar screening?

options.A: A young child recovering from a normal cold
options.B: A healthy athlete with mild muscle soreness after running
options.C: An adult with obesity and a family history of diabetes
options.D: An elderly patient admitted with a broken bone from a fall

explanation: Great thinking! People with risk factors like extra weight and a family history are prime candidates for routine checks so we catch issues early. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h2)

question: How many hours of fasting are normally needed before a fasting blood sugar test?
explanation: An 8 to 12 hour fast (usually overnight) gives the body enough time to clear out food from the last meal so we get a true baseline reading. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h3)

question: Why should nurses tell patients not to chew gum or smoke while fasting for this test?

options.A: They mess up the laboratory machine used to spin blood
options.B: They can trigger digestion and change the blood sugar results
options.C: They cause severe dehydration that collapses arm veins
options.D: They immediately destroy all red blood cells in the body

explanation: Even tiny actions like chewing gum can trick the body into releasing insulin, throwing off the test results. Patient instructions matter! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h3)

question: Which color of blood collection tube is normally used for a fasting blood sugar test?
explanation: Easy to remember in the ward! Gray-top tubes are your go-to tubes for blood sugar and glucose tolerance tests. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h4)

question: What is the main job of sodium fluoride inside the blood collection tube?

options.A: It stains white blood cells for the microscope
options.B: It speeds up blood clotting so serum separates instantly
options.C: It stops blood cells from consuming the glucose inside the tube
options.D: It stops the blood sample from freezing during transport

explanation: Think of sodium fluoride as a preservative. Without it, the living blood cells inside the tube would keep eating up the glucose, giving you a falsely low lab result! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h4)

question: Which fasting blood sugar level is usually the cutoff for diagnosing diabetes mellitus?
explanation: Keep this number handy for your clinical postings: 126 mg/dL or higher on two separate tests points toward a diabetes diagnosis. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h5)

question: A patient's fasting blood sugar comes back at 115 mg/dL. How should you interpret this?

options.B: It is a completely normal result
options.C: It indicates prediabetes and impaired fasting glucose
options.D: It shows the patient had severe low blood sugar

explanation: Values between 100 and 125 mg/dL sit in the prediabetic zone. It's a great warning sign for patients to adjust their diet and lifestyle early! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h5)

question: Why can a sudden infection or severe physical stress cause a high fasting blood sugar reading?

options.A: White blood cells make sugar to fight germs
options.B: Stress hormones like cortisol and adrenaline raise blood sugar
options.C: Infection stops the kidneys from filtering glucose
options.D: Fever destroys insulin receptors in the muscles

explanation: When the body is under stress or fighting sickness, it pumps out emergency hormones (like cortisol) that naturally push blood sugar up to give the body quick energy. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h6)

question: Which of the following does NOT falsely alter a fasting blood sugar result?

options.C: Taking steroid medications in the morning
options.D: Drinking plain water during the fast

explanation: Plain water is totally fine! It has no sugar or calories, so drinking it won't ruin your patient's lab test. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h6)

question: What is a key nursing duty right before a patient takes a fasting blood sugar test?

options.A: Confirming that the patient actually followed the fasting rules
options.B: Giving the patient a small snack to boost energy
options.C: Checking their urine output with a dipstick
options.D: Giving a quick dose of insulin just in case

explanation: Always double-check! Asking 'When was your last meal or drink?' ensures you don't send inaccurate lab samples to the path lab. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h7)

question: A patient waiting for a fasting blood sugar test looks pale, shaky, and dizzy. What should you do first?

options.A: Ask the lab tech to draw their blood right now
options.B: Give them a cup of hot black coffee with sugar
options.C: Check their blood sugar level immediately for low blood sugar
options.D: Tell them to keep waiting patiently for their turn

explanation: Safety first! Shaking, dizziness, and paleness during a fast are classic signs of hypoglycemia. Assess their blood sugar right away before doing anything else. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h7)
